stories.h: BREAKING: Court sacks Uzodimma as APC senatorial candidate for Imo West, orders INEC to recognise Okorocha
stories.p: A Federal High Court in Abuja has ruled that Governor Hope Uzodimma did not win the APC primary for the Imo West Senate seat and that former governor Rochas Okorocha polled the most votes. The court ordered INEC to publish Okorocha as the party's candidate and barred Uzodimma from presenting himself as the candidate.
body: The political battle in Imo State has taken a dramatic turn after a Federal High Court in Abuja ruled that Governor Hope Uzodimma is not the All Progressives Congress (APC) candidate for the Imo West senatorial seat.

In a judgment delivered on Thursday, Justice Obiora Egwuatu held that Uzodimma did not win the party's May 18 primary for Imo West and that former governor Rochas Okorocha polled the highest votes. The court ordered INEC to recognise Okorocha and publish his name as the APC's candidate, and barred Uzodimma from presenting himself as the party's candidate.

Okorocha filed the suit in August, arguing that INEC's own monitors' reports showed him as the winner of the primary. His camp says he scored 150,780 votes to Uzodimma's 102,158, while the party's returning officer had declared Uzodimma the winner with 230,464 votes. Uzodimma and the APC had asked the court to throw out the case as filed too late.
It is not yet known whether Uzodimma or the APC will appeal.

The ruling raises fresh questions about the balance of power within Imo APC. It comes amid growing political tension involving Governor Uzodimma and FCT Minister Nyesom Wike over cross-party alliances and control of party structures ahead of the 2027 elections. However, there is no evidence that Wike had anything to do with the court's decision.
Is Hope Uzodimma gradually losing his grip on Imo politics, or is this just a temporary setback in the battle for 2027?

stories.h: VeryDarkMan inspects warehouse of his 40ft container of power banks from China, targets students, barbers and makeup artists
stories.p: VeryDarkMan has shown off the warehouse holding his 40-foot container of power banks and portable power stations from China, saying they are aimed at students, barbers, makeup artists and small businesses hit by Nigeria's power cuts. How affordable they turn out to be will decide how many of those customers they reach.
body: Popular Nigerian social media activist and philanthropist Martins Vincent Otse, widely known as VeryDarkMan (VDM), has once again attracted public attention after visiting his warehouse to inspect a shipment of power banks and portable power stations imported from China in a 40-foot container.

During the visit, VDM explained that the products were brought into Nigeria with students, barbers, makeup artists and other small business owners in mind, particularly those who struggle daily with Nigeria's unreliable electricity supply.
According to him, many Nigerians are unable to study comfortably or run their businesses efficiently because of constant power outages.
For students, having a reliable source of electricity can make a difference when preparing for examinations, attending online classes or studying at night.
For barbers and makeup artists, electricity is equally important. Many depend on electrical equipment to earn their daily income, and every hour without power can mean losing customers and money.
VDM believes that making portable power solutions available to these groups could help reduce some of the difficulties they face.
## From social media activism to business

Over the years, VeryDarkMan has built a reputation for speaking out on issues affecting ordinary Nigerians, particularly people who struggle to make ends meet. His latest business venture appears to reflect that same interest in the challenges facing low-income earners.
Rather than concentrating only on luxury products, VDM says he wants to provide practical solutions that students, artisans and small business owners can use in their everyday lives.
However, the prices, capacities and affordability of the imported products will ultimately determine how accessible they are to the people he hopes to serve.
## A business idea that addresses a real Nigerian problem

Nigeria's electricity challenges have continued to place enormous pressure on households and small businesses. Many artisans spend a significant portion of their earnings on fuel, generator maintenance and alternative power sources just to stay in business.
If VDM can offer reliable portable power stations at affordable prices, the venture could become a useful option for people who cannot afford expensive solar installations or large generators.

What makes this development particularly interesting is his stated intention to combine business with solutions to everyday problems. VDM has made it clear that he intends to make money from the venture while providing products that could make life easier for Nigerians.

VDM continues to show an interest in the struggles of ordinary Nigerians, whether through his activism, humanitarian activities or business ventures. His latest move deserves attention, especially if the products eventually reach students and low-income workers at prices they can genuinely afford.
What do you think about VDM's latest business venture? Would you buy an affordable portable power station to support your studies or business?

stories.h: Uzodimma vs Wike? Imo governor rejects Rainbow Coalition, threatens to take back vehicles from APC members who work against the party
stories.p: Imo Governor Hope Uzodimma has reportedly declared there will be "no Rainbow Coalition in Imo State", warning APC members that he will take back vehicles donated by Tompolo from anyone who works outside the party. The remarks are being read as a message to Nyesom Wike's cross-party allies ahead of 2027.
body: Political tension appears to be brewing in Imo State as Governor Hope Uzodimma sends a strong warning to members of the All Progressives Congress (APC), declaring that there is no room for a Rainbow Coalition in the state.
In remarks attributed to the governor, Uzodimma warned APC members against working outside the party's political structure, insisting that loyalty to the APC must remain their priority.

The governor reportedly went further by threatening to withdraw vehicles donated by Niger Delta leader High Chief Government Ekpemupolo, popularly known as Tompolo, from beneficiaries found supporting political arrangements outside the APC.
"No Rainbow Coalition in Imo State. If I see you work outside the APC party, I'll take the vehicles from you," Uzodimma was quoted as saying.
The governor also expressed appreciation to Tompolo for his generosity and pledged his support whenever the Niger Delta leader needed assistance in Imo State.
"I am very grateful to High Chief Tompolo. Anytime you need us in Imo State, let us know and we'll be there for you," he reportedly added.
## Is Uzodimma drawing a political battle line against Wike?

The governor's reported declaration has raised questions about the political influence of the Minister of the Federal Capital Territory, Nyesom Wike, whose name has become associated with cross-party political alliances.

Wike, although a member of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP), serves in President Bola Tinubu's APC-led administration and has maintained political relationships across party lines. His political approach has often involved cooperation between politicians belonging to different parties, particularly in Rivers State.
However, Uzodimma's reported warning suggests that he is unwilling to accommodate a similar arrangement within the Imo APC.
Although the remarks could be interpreted as a message to Wike's political allies, they do not, on their own, establish that the two politicians are in a direct confrontation.
## Questions over Tompolo's donated vehicles
Another interesting aspect of the governor's reported statement is his warning about withdrawing vehicles donated by Tompolo.

The remarks raise questions about whether the vehicles were intended as unconditional gifts or whether their continued use is tied to political loyalty. It also remains unclear what authority would govern the withdrawal of the vehicles from beneficiaries.
## What does this mean for Imo politics?

With political calculations already taking shape ahead of the 2027 general elections, Uzodimma's reported position could signal an attempt to strengthen party discipline and prevent competing political alliances from gaining influence within the state.
For now, the bigger question is whether the governor's declaration is simply an internal warning to APC members or the beginning of a wider struggle over political influence.
One thing is certain: if these remarks are accurately reported, Governor Hope Uzodimma has made his position clear. He expects APC members in Imo State to remain loyal to the party.

But should vehicles donated to politicians be withdrawn simply because the beneficiaries choose to support a different political alliance? And could this be the beginning of a political disagreement between Uzodimma and Wike ahead of 2027?

stories.h: No permanent enemies, only permanent interests! Hilda Dokubo reportedly visits Wike, with Kingsley Chinda present
stories.p: Nollywood veteran and activist Hilda Dokubo, long seen as a strong critic of FCT Minister Nyesom Wike, has reportedly visited him at his Port Harcourt home, with Wike ally Kingsley Chinda also present. Nobody outside the meeting knows what was discussed, but it has raised questions about a possible reconciliation or new alliance ahead of 2027.
body: Nigerian politics will teach you lessons that no university can offer!

Nollywood veteran and political activist Hilda Dokubo, who has previously been associated with strong opposition to FCT Minister Nyesom Wike, has reportedly visited him at his Port Harcourt residence.

This is the same Hilda Dokubo whom critics have accused of making hostile remarks about Wike and of supporting groups that displayed his obituary on a coffin during political protests. Those allegations remain unverified.
Now, reports of a meeting between the two have raised eyebrows, especially because of the presence of Kingsley Chinda, a prominent Rivers politician widely regarded as a Wike ally.
The big question is: what could these three political figures be discussing behind closed doors?
Is this political reconciliation? A fresh alliance ahead of the 2027 elections? Or another example of the famous Nigerian political principle, "scratch my back, and I will scratch yours"?

Of course, nobody outside that meeting can say for certain what was discussed. But considering the bitter political disagreements that have characterised Rivers State politics, the reported gathering is bound to generate questions.
It is a reminder for Nigerians to be careful about fighting, insulting and destroying relationships because of politicians.
Today, two politicians are sworn enemies. Tomorrow, they are sitting in the same living room, smiling, shaking hands and possibly negotiating their next political move.
Meanwhile, their supporters are still fighting yesterday's battles on Facebook!

Never gamble your peace, friendships or future on the political quarrels of Nigerian politicians and their celebrity supporters. In Nigerian politics, today's enemy can become tomorrow's political partner.
What do you think brought Hilda Dokubo, Wike and Kingsley Chinda together? Reconciliation, political calculation or something else?

stories.h: Emotional moment boy collapses after his mother surprises him at school following four years abroad
stories.p: A young boy reportedly collapsed with emotion when his mother, who had been living abroad for four years, turned up unannounced at his school. The video of their reunion has touched many online and sparked a conversation about the price families pay when parents travel abroad for a better future.
body: An emotional reunion between a mother and her son has captured attention on social media after the young boy reportedly collapsed upon seeing his mother for the first time in four years.
According to the story accompanying the circulating video, the woman had been living abroad for four years, leaving her son behind while she pursued a better future for her family.
After years of separation, she decided to return home and surprise her son at his school without telling him she was coming.
What was supposed to be a joyful reunion quickly became an overwhelming moment for the young boy.
Upon seeing his mother unexpectedly, the boy reportedly became so overwhelmed that he collapsed, leaving those around him concerned.

The touching scene has sparked emotional reactions online, with many social media users reflecting on the sacrifices parents make when they travel abroad in search of better opportunities for their children.

For many families, living abroad comes with a painful price. Parents sometimes spend years away from their children, missing birthdays, school activities, family celebrations and important childhood moments.
Although financial support can help provide a better life, the emotional impact of prolonged separation can be difficult for both parents and children.
The circumstances surrounding the boy's reported collapse, including whether he needed medical attention, have not been independently confirmed.
Nevertheless, the reunion has reminded many people of the importance of family, parental presence and the emotional bond between mothers and their children.
Four years without seeing his mother, and suddenly she appeared right before his eyes. Imagine the emotions running through that little boy's heart.
What do you think about parents leaving their young children behind for several years to work abroad in search of a better future? Is the sacrifice worth it?

stories.h: Rivers politics: Fubara backs Wike's cross-party Rainbow Coalition and its 2027 candidates
stories.p: Governor Siminalayi Fubara has publicly pledged support for President Tinubu, Nyesom Wike and the seven-party Rainbow Coalition, which has unveiled Kingsley Chinda and Major Jack of the APC as its governorship ticket. The move shows the former rivals now campaigning in the same bloc, though a court challenge to Chinda's eligibility is still pending.
body: Governor Siminalayi Fubara has publicly pledged support for President Tinubu, Nyesom Wike and the Rainbow Coalition's 2027 candidates in Rivers State. The seven-party alliance unveiled Kingsley Chinda and Major Jack, both of the APC, as its governorship and deputy governorship choices. The rest of its slate combines APC and PDP candidates.
## Why it is trending

"Rainbow Coalition" entered Nigeria's trending topics on X. The unveiling confirms that Fubara and Wike are now openly campaigning within the same political bloc after their long-running disagreement.
## What has changed
The reconciliation has moved from meetings and public statements to a jointly supported electoral slate. The coalition adopted:
Kingsley Chinda and Major Jack for governor and deputy governor.
Two APC and one PDP senatorial candidates.
Ten APC and three PDP House of Representatives candidates.
Twenty-one APC and eleven PDP State Assembly candidates.
## Still uncertain

A court challenge to Chinda's eligibility remains unresolved, with a hearing reportedly scheduled for 4 November 2026. The September Supreme Court decision at the centre of the dispute did not specifically disqualify Chinda, and rival groups disagree over what it means. The coalition's endorsement therefore does not settle the pending legal question.

stories.h: "I have lost everything I worked for, I am starting afresh" – Blessing CEO breaks down in tears as she recounts losing her son and her time in custody
stories.p: Relationship therapist Blessing CEO has broken down in tears while talking about losing her son and her time in detention, saying she has lost almost everything she built and must start again. She also said she is ready to look at her past mistakes and take a different path in life.
body: Controversial Nigerian relationship therapist and social media personality Blessing CEO has sparked emotional reactions after breaking down in tears while recounting some of the most painful experiences of her life, including the loss of her son and her time in custody.

In an emotional account, Blessing opened up about the personal struggles she has endured, revealing that her experiences have forced her to reflect deeply on her life, decisions and the direction she wants to take going forward.
According to her, she has lost virtually everything she spent years working to build and is now faced with the difficult task of starting all over again.
One of the most touching moments came when she spoke about losing her son, an experience that appeared to leave her overwhelmed with grief.
She also reflected on her time in detention and how it affected her emotionally and personally.
However, what caught the attention of many was her willingness to examine her past actions and acknowledge that there may be areas where she got things wrong.
Blessing expressed her readiness to identify her mistakes, make necessary corrections and take a different path in life.

For someone who has built a public image around controversial opinions, outspoken statements and heated social media exchanges, her emotional reflections have introduced another side of her personality to the public.
She now appears determined to rebuild her life, even if it means starting from nothing.
Her story raises important questions about personal growth, forgiveness and second chances. Can someone who has made mistakes in the past genuinely change and rebuild their life?

Whatever opinions people may have about Blessing CEO, watching someone speak about losing a child, being locked up and watching years of hard work disappear is a reminder that public figures also face painful personal struggles.
Do you believe Blessing CEO deserves a second chance, or do you think she still has a lot to prove to Nigerians?

stories.h: BREAKING: Police arrest Umar Ibrahim Gandi over viral video calling for AK-47s to attack worshippers in Enugu and Jos

Police say he faces allegations of incitement to violence, disturbance of public peace and criminal intimidation, and will be charged in court. JIBWIS has disassociated itself from his conduct.
body: The Zamfara State Police Command has arrested Umar Ibrahim Gandi, the man seen in a viral video calling for AK-47 rifles to carry out attacks against Christians in Enugu State and Jos, Plateau State.

Police identified the suspect as a 22-year-old native of Maradun Local Government Area of Zamfara State. They say the video was recorded on Friday, October 23, 2026, and that he faces allegations of incitement to violence, disturbance of public peace and criminal intimidation. The Commissioner of Police said an investigation is under way and that the suspect will be charged before a court.

In the video, the suspect, wearing the uniform of the JIBWIS (Izala) first-aid group, is heard chanting for rifles to kill people he calls "infidels" during Sunday worship. According to the police, JIBWIS has disassociated itself from his alleged conduct.

His statements raised serious concerns about religious extremism, hate speech and threats to innocent lives, and the video attracted widespread condemnation, with many Nigerians calling on the DSS and the police to identify and arrest him.
Particularly troubling was the presence of young children during the recording, raising questions about the exposure of minors to violent extremist messages.
Nigerians will now expect a thorough investigation and appropriate legal action based on the evidence. Like any suspect, he is presumed innocent until proven guilty in court.

Nigeria cannot afford to treat public threats of violence against religious communities as ordinary social media content. Nobody should be threatened with death simply because of where they come from or how they worship God.

body: Taylor Jasmine, the girlfriend of popular Nigerian comedian and content creator Carter Efe, has stirred reactions on social media after expressing her sadness over her planned return to the United States.

I'll be back soon," she wrote, adding in another post: "I don't wanna go back home. The fact I'm leaving tomorrow. I'm crying. I had some fun out here, man."
Her words have attracted attention online, with many Nigerians reacting to her apparent love for the country and the experiences she has enjoyed during her stay.

For someone who has experienced life in both America and Nigeria, her reluctance to leave has also sparked conversations about the things that make Nigeria special despite its numerous economic and social challenges.

Nigeria may be facing difficulties, but its vibrant entertainment industry, rich culture, lively social atmosphere and welcoming communities continue to attract visitors from different parts of the world.
Her relationship with Carter Efe has also placed her in the spotlight, with social media users following their activities and interactions.
While she has expressed her reluctance to leave, it remains unclear whether she intends to extend her stay or proceed with her planned journey to America.

The development has once again highlighted how Nigeria continues to leave lasting impressions on visitors, particularly those who develop personal relationships and meaningful connections during their stay.

body: Fresh concerns have emerged over the welfare of popular Nollywood actor Jerry Williams after filmmaker and producer Izutech publicly questioned the Actors Guild of Nigeria (AGN) over its alleged failure to provide sustained support for the troubled actor.
According to Izutech, the Actors Guild of Nigeria had previously promised to take responsibility for Jerry Williams' situation, but he is now questioning what became of that commitment.

Expressing his disappointment, Izutech questioned why an actor who contributed to Nigeria's entertainment industry should allegedly be left struggling without adequate support.
He also disclosed his willingness to intervene again by arranging a rehabilitation programme lasting up to two years, which he believes could help the actor recover and rebuild his life.
However, the producer admitted that such an intervention would require considerable financial resources and appealed for support from colleagues, industry stakeholders and well-meaning Nigerians.

The development has once again brought attention to the welfare of entertainers in Nollywood, especially actors facing health challenges, financial difficulties or personal crises after years in the spotlight.
It also raises questions about the responsibility of professional associations to support members experiencing serious difficulties.

While Izutech's allegations have attracted concern, the actor's current medical condition and the extent of any assistance provided by the Actors Guild of Nigeria have not been independently verified.
The bigger question remains: what support systems are available to Nollywood actors when they can no longer cope with life's challenges?

stories.h: INEC under fire over alleged AI-generated images in voter register as concerns grow over Nigeria's democracy
stories.p: INEC is facing criticism after users shared screenshots of entries in the newly published preliminary voter register, mainly from Edo State, whose photos they say appear to be AI-generated. Pat Utomi has asked the commission to explain, and some users also allege duplicate entries. INEC had not publicly responded to the claims, which have not been independently verified.
body: Fresh concerns have emerged over the credibility of Nigeria's Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) following allegations that AI-generated images were found in the preliminary voter register, raising serious questions about the integrity of the country's electoral system.

The claims surfaced after INEC uploaded the preliminary register online, with users sharing screenshots of entries from several polling units in Edo State whose photographs they say look artificially generated. Some users have also alleged duplicate entries with the same photograph under different voter numbers. Economist and politician Pat Utomi has publicly asked INEC to explain the images. INEC had not publicly responded to the specific allegations at the time of writing.
The allegations have sparked concerns about the effectiveness of INEC's verification procedures, transparency and accountability, particularly as Nigeria prepares for future elections.

For an institution entrusted with protecting the voting rights of millions of Nigerians, the possibility of AI-generated photographs appearing in an official electoral database is a matter that deserves urgent investigation.
If confirmed, such irregularities could expose serious weaknesses in the processes used to register voters, authenticate their identities and maintain accurate electoral records.
How can Nigerians trust an electoral system if the authenticity of the photographs and identities contained in its register cannot be guaranteed?

INEC has a constitutional responsibility to conduct credible elections and maintain a reliable register of eligible voters. Any failure to detect manipulated images or questionable registrations could further weaken public confidence in an institution that has faced criticism over previous electoral exercises.

The growing sophistication of artificial intelligence also presents new challenges for electoral authorities worldwide. Images that appear genuine can now be generated or manipulated using readily available technology, making strong identity verification procedures increasingly important.

However, the existence of suspicious images alone would not establish electoral fraud. A proper investigation would need to determine whether the photographs were genuinely AI-generated, how they entered the register and whether they were connected to valid voter records.

Nigerians deserve clear answers from INEC. The commission should establish the facts, explain its verification procedures and disclose what safeguards are in place to prevent fraudulent registrations and manipulation of electoral information.
Where wrongdoing is established, those responsible should be identified and held accountable under the law.

Nigeria cannot afford another election overshadowed by doubts about the credibility of the electoral process. Democracy depends on public confidence that every legitimate vote will count and that electoral institutions can protect the integrity of the process.
With the 2027 general elections approaching, INEC must demonstrate that its systems are secure, its records are reliable and its operations are open to independent scrutiny.
The credibility of Nigeria's democracy is too important to be left to assumptions, political assurances or unanswered allegations.

The question Nigerians are asking is simple: if INEC cannot guarantee the authenticity of the identities in its electoral register, how can citizens be confident that it will deliver free, fair and credible elections in 2027?

body: The Federal Government is reportedly considering legislation that would protect key economic reforms introduced under President Bola Ahmed Tinubu from being easily reversed by future administrations.

stories.h: Wike reportedly promises Tinubu appointment for PDP candidate who stepped down for APC
stories.p: FCT Minister Nyesom Wike has reportedly pledged a federal appointment from President Tinubu to a PDP candidate who withdrew from a race in favour of the APC candidate. The reported promise is likely to draw reaction from opposition parties ahead of 2027.
more: Opposition parties are yet to respond to the reported pledge.
The details of the post on offer have not been disclosed.

stories.h: 2Baba says he is 'a changed man' as family saga with Natasha Osawaru continues
stories.p: Singer 2Baba has reportedly opened up on a new personal resolution while the dispute involving his family and Natasha Osawaru continues to attract public attention. He is said to have described himself as a changed man.
more: The singer's family situation has been in the news for months.
Fans are divided in their reactions online.
stories.credit: Photo: One Africa Music Fest / Wikimedia Commons, CC BY 3.0

stories.h: Trump reportedly offers $1 million rewards for tips on voter fraud in US elections
stories.p: US President Donald Trump has reportedly said the government will pay $1 million for information that leads to proof of voter fraud. The announcement is said to have come as the American political season heats up.
more: Critics are expected to question how such rewards would be verified and funded.
No official guidance on how to claim the reward has been reported yet.
stories.credit: Photo: Shealeah Craighead / Wikimedia Commons, Public domain

stories.h: Iyabo Ojo and Paulo's sweet exchange gets fans talking amid rumours of a new man
stories.p: A friendly public exchange between Nollywood actress Iyabo Ojo and Paulo has caught the attention of fans, who are linking it to rumours that she has a new partner. Neither has confirmed any relationship.
more: Fans have flooded the comment section with guesses.
Iyabo Ojo has not addressed the rumours directly.
stories.credit: Photo: Danielle G. Campbell / Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 4.0

stories.h: Troops reportedly arrest suspected militia member who is a youth chairman in Plateau's Mangu
stories.p: Soldiers have reportedly arrested a suspected militia member, said to be a youth chairman in Mangu, Plateau State, after a clash in the area. Further details on the case have not yet been released.
more: The area has seen repeated security incidents in recent months.
Authorities have not said what charges the suspect may face.

stories.h: Nigerian buy-now-pay-later company reportedly shuts down after several years
stories.p: A Nigerian company offering buy-now-pay-later services has reportedly closed its doors after several years in operation. Customers with outstanding balances are said to be awaiting guidance.
more: Users are advised to watch for official notices on repayments.
The firm's reasons for closing are said to be commercial.

stories.h: NCDC warns 2027 elections could be postponed if Ebola spreads widely
stories.p: The Nigeria Centre for Disease Control has reportedly said the 2027 general elections could be postponed if Ebola spreads widely across the country. The warning comes as Nigeria has no active confirmed case but has not yet been declared Ebola-free. The health minister earlier said the country could declare itself Ebola-free from 7 December.
more: The WHO says Nigeria has no active case but is not yet declared Ebola-free.
The health minister has pointed to 7 December as a possible date for the declaration.
Election timetables have drawn plenty of attention as campaigns gather pace.

stories.h: Mr Eazi says he turned down a Chelsea offer before Mikel Obi joined the club
stories.p: Singer and entrepreneur Mr Eazi has reportedly said, in a video, that he rejected an offer connected to Chelsea before Mikel Obi signed for the English club. The remark has drawn fresh attention from music and football fans online.
more: Mikel Obi went on to become one of the best-known Nigerians in the Premier League.
Mr Eazi has often spoken about his love of football.
Fans have been trading reactions on social media.

stories.h: Judy Austin reacts after Yul Edochie shares throwback clips featuring May
stories.p: Judy Austin has reportedly reacted to throwback videos posted by actor Yul Edochie that feature his first wife, May. The reaction has sparked debate among fans online about the long-running family saga.
more: Yul Edochie recently shared old clips from his earlier years with May.
The saga has remained a frequent talking point on Nigerian social media.
Neither side has said more beyond the online reactions.

stories.h: Obi cautions against harassing his supporters, says no one holds a monopoly on wrongdoing
stories.p: Peter Obi has reportedly urged people not to harass his supporters, saying arrogance does not pay and that no one has a monopoly on wrongdoing. The NDC candidate spoke as the 2027 campaign heats up between the main parties.
more: Obi leads the NDC ticket alongside Rabiu Kwankwaso.
The party recently unveiled its 2027 campaign council.
The APC and ADC are also pushing their own campaigns.

stories.h: First Lady Oluremi Tinubu commissions national headquarters of Tompolo-backed PBAT movement in Abuja
stories.p: First Lady Oluremi Tinubu has reportedly opened the national headquarters of the PBAT Door-to-Door Movement in Abuja, a group linked to Tompolo and supporting President Tinubu's re-election bid. The event is part of the APC's growing 2027 campaign push.
more: Tompolo has reportedly donated campaign vehicles for the re-election drive in Adamawa.
The APC recently inaugurated its presidential campaign council.
Opposition parties are running their own campaign structures.

stories.h: Dubai plans world's longest 24-karat gold walkway before the end of the year
stories.p: Dubai is reportedly planning to open what it describes as the world's longest walkway decorated in 24-karat gold before the year ends. The plan has drawn wide attention online as a showpiece for the city's tourism push.
more: Dubai regularly unveils record-setting attractions.
Social media users have shared jokes about walking on gold.
Further details are expected closer to the opening.

stories.h: Alex Otti praised for honouring Nollywood legend Zebrudaya with ₦10 million and a car as Anambra government faces criticism
stories.p: Veteran actor Tony Akposheri has praised Abia State Governor Alex Otti for reportedly honouring Chief Chika Okpala, the comedy legend known as Zebrudaya, with ₦10 million and a car. Akposheri questioned why Anambra State, where Zebrudaya comes from, has not given him similar recognition.
body: Veteran Nollywood actor and entertainment personality Ambassador Tony Akposheri has praised Abia State Governor Alex Otti for reportedly honouring legendary Nigerian comedian and actor Chief Chika Okpala, popularly known as Zebrudaya, with a gift of ₦10 million and a car.

Akposheri expressed disappointment that Zebrudaya, who hails from Nnobi in Anambra State, has allegedly not received similar recognition from his home state despite his enormous contributions to Nigeria's entertainment industry.

According to the veteran actor, it is remarkable that a governor from another state has chosen to celebrate a man whose talent and creativity helped shape Nigerian television entertainment for generations.
## Zebrudaya: a legend who entertained generations of Nigerians
Chief Chika Okpala became a household name through his unforgettable portrayal of Chief Zebrudaya Okoroigwe Nwogbo, alias 4.30, in the popular Nigerian television comedy series New Masquerade.
The programme was one of Nigeria's most celebrated television productions, entertaining millions of families across the country during the 1970s, 1980s and beyond.
With his distinctive command of English, humorous expressions, traditional attire and remarkable comic timing, Zebrudaya became one of the most recognisable characters in Nigerian television history.
For many Nigerians who grew up watching New Masquerade, Zebrudaya represents an important part of their childhood memories and the golden era of Nigerian television.
His contributions helped establish comedy as a respected form of entertainment long before the emergence of today's Nollywood industry and modern stand-up comedy scene.
## Tony Akposheri questions Anambra State's recognition of its own legend
Reacting to Governor Otti's reported gesture, Akposheri questioned why the Anambra State Government had not adequately celebrated a personality of Zebrudaya's standing.
He argued that individuals who dedicated decades of their lives to entertaining Nigerians deserve recognition and appreciation while they are still alive.

Akposheri stated: "Zebrudaya is from Nnobi, Anambra State, but the Anambra State Government has not recognised or celebrated him for his contributions to the entertainment industry. Instead, it was Alex Otti, the governor of Abia State, who recently celebrated him with a gift of ₦10 million and a car.
"God bless Alex Otti! I wish other governors could replicate what Alex Otti is doing by honouring our legends who put smiles on our faces during our childhood."
His remarks have brought attention to the wider issue of how Nigerian society recognises veteran entertainers who contributed to the growth of the country's creative industry.
## Otti's gesture sparks conversation about celebrating living legends
Governor Alex Otti's reported gesture has been described by Akposheri as an example of the importance of appreciating distinguished Nigerians regardless of their states of origin.
The recognition also raises an important question about the responsibility of state governments to preserve their cultural and entertainment heritage.

Across Nigeria, several veteran actors, musicians and comedians have spent decades building careers that influenced younger generations of entertainers. Yet concerns persist about whether these pioneers receive sufficient institutional recognition and support, particularly as they grow older.

For many observers, honouring entertainment veterans should go beyond financial gifts. It could include lifetime achievement awards, cultural preservation projects, healthcare support and programmes documenting their contributions to Nigerian history.
## Should state governments do more for veteran entertainers?

Akposheri's comments have reopened discussions about the need for Nigerian governors to celebrate distinguished citizens who have made lasting contributions to entertainment, education, sports and other areas of national development.

While Zebrudaya's reported recognition by the Abia State Governor has attracted praise, Akposheri's criticism of the Anambra State Government remains his personal assessment. The state's full record of honours or recognition for the veteran actor has not been established in this report.
For generations of Nigerians, Chief Chika Okpala remains a treasured figure whose performances brought laughter into countless homes.

The question now is whether other state governors will follow Governor Otti's reported example by celebrating Nigeria's surviving entertainment pioneers while they are still alive to enjoy the recognition.
What is your opinion? Should the Anambra State Government do more to honour Zebrudaya, or should recognition of national legends go beyond their states of origin?

stories.h: Kylian Mbappé responds after losing the 2026 Ballon d'Or to Harry Kane
stories.p: Kylian Mbappé has reportedly reacted to missing out on the 2026 Ballon d'Or, which went to England captain Harry Kane. The France forward finished behind Kane in the voting at the London ceremony. His response has drawn plenty of attention from football fans online.
more: Kane became the first Englishman to win the award in 25 years.
Lamine Yamal was also among the leading names in the voting.
The organisers earlier apologised after the winners were published by mistake.

stories.h: Naira posts fresh losses as CBN adjusts the dollar rate, despite $55.2bn in reserves
stories.p: The Central Bank of Nigeria has adjusted its official dollar exchange rate, and the naira has recorded fresh losses. This comes even though the country's foreign reserves are reported at $55.2 billion. Analysts are watching how the currency moves in the coming days.
more: Reserves of $55.2bn are among the highest in recent years.
The naira has been under pressure in the official market this week.

stories.h: FCCPC updates its list of approved loan apps, highlighting five platforms for salary earners
stories.p: Nigeria's consumer protection regulator has refreshed its list of loan apps, highlighting five platforms said to offer salary earners as much as N10 million. The update is meant to help borrowers pick registered lenders rather than unlicensed ones.
more: Borrowers are urged to check that an app is on the official list before sharing personal data.
Unregistered loan apps have faced complaints over harassment and hidden charges.

stories.h: Dispute over burial of singer Toluwanising continues as relatives and supporters weigh in
stories.p: A disagreement over the burial of singer Toluwanising is reportedly playing out online. An uncle is said to have asked that he should not be buried yet, while others have come out to defend his widow and ask that she be allowed to mourn in peace.
more: Wale Jana reportedly said a man should not be buried in the only house he built, while the singer's grandmother insists he be buried in it.
The uncle has also spoken about what he found at the singer's home after his death.
No official family statement has been shared publicly yet.

stories.h: Tinubu gives Festus Keyamo a fresh appointment
stories.p: President Bola Tinubu has reportedly handed Aviation Minister Festus Keyamo a new appointment. Details of the new role are expected to be spelt out by the presidency.
more: Keyamo is one of the more visible ministers in the cabinet.

stories.h: WHO says Nigeria has no active Ebola case but has not yet been declared Ebola-free
stories.p: The World Health Organization has clarified that Nigeria currently has no active confirmed Ebola case, but the country has not been formally declared Ebola-free. The clarification follows talk that Nigeria could make the declaration from 7 December.
more: The health minister earlier suggested the country could declare itself Ebola-free on 7 December.
Surveillance continues while the countdown runs.

stories.h: Jasmine Taylor gushes over Carter Efe: "I found someone who does the most with me"
stories.p: Jasmine Taylor has reportedly praised her partner, skit maker and streamer Carter Efe, saying she has found someone who does the most with her. The remarks have attracted warm and teasing reactions from fans.
more: The couple often feature each other in content online.

stories.h: Man remanded in Kuje over alleged threat to leak Kano Governor Yusuf's private images
stories.p: A Federal High Court in Abuja has remanded Sanusi Dankaka at Kuje Correctional Centre over an alleged threat to leak private images of Kano State Governor Abba Yusuf. The case will continue at a later date.
more: The defendant is said to have been remanded pending further court proceedings.

stories.h: Nigerians allegedly busted for producing fake R100 notes in South Africa
stories.p: Reports claim that Nigerian nationals in South Africa were caught allegedly producing counterfeit R100 banknotes, sparking concern about fake money in circulation. The location, number of suspects and details of any arrest have not been independently verified, and no official statement has been confirmed.
body: A suspected counterfeit currency operation involving Nigerian nationals in South Africa has sparked reactions following reports that individuals were caught allegedly producing fake R100 banknotes.
The incident has raised fresh concerns about counterfeit money circulating in South Africa and the possible consequences for unsuspecting businesses and members of the public.

According to claims surrounding the incident, the individuals were allegedly involved in producing counterfeit South African R100 notes, which could potentially be passed off as genuine currency during everyday transactions.
However, the exact location of the alleged operation, the number of suspects involved, and the circumstances surrounding their reported arrest have yet to be independently verified.

Counterfeit money poses a serious threat to businesses, particularly small traders, street vendors, transport operators and shop owners who handle cash transactions daily. When fake banknotes enter circulation, unsuspecting individuals may accept them as payment, only to discover later that the money has no value.

The alleged involvement of foreign nationals could also fuel tensions in a country where immigration and crime remain sensitive public issues. However, criminal responsibility rests with the individuals involved, and allegations against particular suspects should not be used to generalise about Nigerians living and working legally in South Africa.
Under South African law, producing, possessing or distributing counterfeit currency can attract serious criminal penalties. If the allegations are confirmed, those involved could face prosecution.
No official statement from the authorities detailing the alleged operation, the evidence recovered or any charges filed has been independently confirmed.

The reported incident has prompted questions about how counterfeit currency operations are detected and what measures can protect ordinary people from accepting fake money. It also highlights the importance of checking banknotes carefully, particularly when handling large amounts of cash.
What do you think should be done to tackle counterfeit currency operations in South Africa and protect innocent businesses from financial losses?
stories.alt: A man being handcuffed by South African police, beside R100 banknotes spread out in an open black bag

stories.h: FBI reportedly arrests nine Nigerians in cybercrime operation targeting Americans
stories.p: US authorities have reportedly arrested nine Nigerians wanted over online fraud schemes that targeted American victims. Dozens of phones and computers were said to have been seized in the operation. Details of the charges and where the suspects will face court have not been fully released.
more: About 53 devices were reportedly seized during the arrests.
The FBI has in recent weeks published names and photos of wanted Nigerian fraud suspects.
The suspects are expected to answer to charges in the United States.
stories.credit: Stock image: Noah Wulf / Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 4.0

stories.h: CBN gives JPMorgan approval in principle to open a merchant bank in Nigeria
stories.p: The Central Bank of Nigeria has granted JPMorgan approval in principle to set up JPMorgan Merchant Bank Nigeria Limited. Adedapo Olagunju, who has led the bank's West African operations since 2018, has been cleared to run it. The approval is only a first step, as a final licence is still needed before the bank can begin business.
more: JPMorgan reportedly placed about $38 million with the central bank as a capital deposit.
Board nominees, including independent directors, were also approved.
The firm still has to complete registration with the Corporate Affairs Commission.

stories.h: Combined wealth of Dangote, Rabiu and Otedola reportedly rises to $73.1 billion
stories.p: The combined fortunes of Nigeria's richest businessmen, Aliko Dangote, Abdulsamad Rabiu and Femi Otedola, have reportedly climbed to about $73.1 billion. The rise is said to be driven by gains in their listed companies and refining and energy interests.
more: Dangote remains the richest of the three by a wide margin.
The figures are estimates and move with share prices and exchange rates.
stories.credit: Photo: World Economic Forum / Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 2.0

stories.h: Nigeria shines at the Ballon d'Or as Burna Boy presents the Sócrates Award to Bukayo Saka
stories.p: Afrobeats superstar Burna Boy presented the Sócrates Award to Arsenal and England star Bukayo Saka at the Ballon d'Or ceremony in London on Monday night. The award recognises footballers who make a positive impact on society through humanitarian and community work. It was a proud moment for Nigerian music and football on the global stage.
more: Burna Boy became the first Nigerian artiste to present an award at the Ballon d'Or, which was held in London for the first time.
Saka, who is of Nigerian descent, was honoured for his work with the BigShoe charity, which has funded surgeries for children in Nigeria.
In his speech, Saka read a letter from a 14-year-old boy whose life was changed by the charity.
stories.alt: Four photos from the Ballon d'Or: Burna Boy and Bukayo Saka at the podium with the Sócrates Award, Burna Boy on the red carpet, and the two embracing on stage
stories.credit: Image: social media

stories.h: Umahi questions why Igbos should be given only four years, as others had eight
stories.p: Ebonyi Governor David Umahi has reportedly reacted to Peter Obi's presidential push by asking why Igbos should do only four years when other regions have held power for eight. The remark is drawing reactions from supporters of Obi and of the ruling APC.
more: Obi, the NDC candidate, has previously spoken of serving a single term if elected.
The comment adds to the debate over zoning and the South-East's place in the 2027 race.
stories.credit: Photo: VirtualWinnie / Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 4.0

stories.h: Soludo reportedly says APGA will not automatically back Obi in 2027, urges Igbo unity and wider alliances
stories.p: Anambra Governor Chukwuma Soludo has reportedly said his party, APGA, will not automatically throw its weight behind Peter Obi's 2027 bid. He is said to have called for Igbo unity and broader political alliances instead.
more: Some Igbo groups have already rejected moves by Soludo and APGA to endorse President Tinubu.
Obi's camp has not yet responded in detail.
stories.credit: Photo: Chinedueri / Wikimedia Commons, CC BY 4.0

stories.h: NDC sacks Borno House of Assembly candidate Mohammed Bunu over alleged anti-party activities
stories.p: The Nigeria Democratic Congress has reportedly removed Mohammed Bunu as its candidate for a Borno State House of Assembly seat, accusing him of anti-party activities ahead of the 2027 election.
more: The party is expected to name a replacement ahead of the INEC deadline.
The move comes as the NDC unveils its national campaign council.

stories.h: More than 40 people feared dead after armed attacks on Orthodox churches and villages in Ethiopia
stories.p: Armed attackers have reportedly struck Orthodox Christian churches and nearby villages in Ethiopia, leaving more than 40 people feared dead. Details of who was behind the attacks have not been confirmed.
more: Local reports say worshippers were among the victims.
Authorities are yet to give a full account of the casualties.

stories.h: Asake leaves Paris's Accor Arena hand in hand with his mother after final tour show, and the clip trends
stories.p: A clip of Asake walking out of the Accor Arena in Paris hand in hand with his mother after his last show on the tour is trending, with fans praising the moment.
more: The Paris concert was part of his In God We Trust world tour.
Fans have flooded social media with messages for his mother.
stories.credit: Photo: Mensah Memories / Wikimedia Commons, CC BY 3.0

stories.h: BBNaija's Mercedes reportedly appeals to Don Jazzy for help, says she is not chasing a lavish lifestyle
stories.p: BBNaija's Mercedes has reportedly appealed to Don Jazzy for assistance while insisting she is not chasing a lavish lifestyle. The plea follows reports that the music executive recently announced a tech scholarship and gave out money.
more: Don Jazzy has not publicly responded so far.
Reactions online are split between sympathy and criticism.

stories.h: Rudeboy says going solo after P-Square was easy because he already handled production and songwriting
stories.p: Paul Okoye, known as Rudeboy, has explained that leaving P-Square for a solo career came easily because he was already involved in production and songwriting during the group's years.
more: He has built a solo catalogue since the group split.
He did not say whether a reunion is planned.
stories.credit: Photo: Accelerate TV / Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 4.0

stories.h: Court reportedly orders El-Rufai to enter his defence in the phone-tapping trial
stories.p: A Federal High Court in Abuja has reportedly rejected former Kaduna governor Nasir El-Rufai's no-case submission, meaning he must now present a defence. The DSS is prosecuting him on a five-count charge over alleged unlawful interception of communications.
more: The ruling followed arguments from both sides on whether the prosecution had made out a prima facie case.
El-Rufai remains in custody after an earlier bail variation request was refused.
stories.credit: Photo: VOA / Wikimedia Commons, Public domain

stories.h: Burna Boy presents the Socrates Award to Bukayo Saka at the Ballon d'Or ceremony in London
stories.p: Nigerian superstar Burna Boy handed the Socrates Award to Arsenal and England winger Bukayo Saka on stage at the 2026 Ballon d'Or ceremony in London. The moment drew warm reactions from football and music fans online.
more: The ceremony in London also crowned Harry Kane as the 2026 winner.
Saka was honoured for his work off the pitch.
stories.credit: Photo: Nuță Lucian / Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 2.0

stories.h: Gunmen reportedly kill 58 people in a four-hour raid on a Taraba community
stories.p: Armed men are said to have attacked a community in Taraba State for about four hours, leaving 58 people dead according to a report. Details on the exact location and who was behind the raid are still limited, and security agencies are yet to give a full account.
more: Reports say the attack lasted around four hours before the gunmen withdrew.
Residents and local leaders are expected to press for stronger security in the area.

stories.h: Islamic cleric Sheikh Yahaya Masusuka reportedly shot dead by gunmen at his home in Katsina
stories.p: Gunmen are said to have killed Sheikh Yahaya Masusuka at his home in Dutsin-Ma, Katsina State, in what is reportedly a targeted attack. Police are yet to say who carried it out or why. The militant group Ansaru has reportedly claimed responsibility, a claim that has not been independently verified.
more: The attack is said to have taken place at the cleric's residence.
Dutsin-Ma has seen repeated security incidents in recent months.
The Katsina state government has reportedly promised action over the killing.

stories.h: Harry Kane wins the 2026 Ballon d'Or, ahead of Lamine Yamal and Kylian Mbappe
stories.p: Harry Kane has been named winner of the 2026 Ballon d'Or at the ceremony in London, becoming the first Englishman to take the award in 25 years. He beat Barcelona's Lamine Yamal and PSG's Kylian Mbappe to the prize. Kane has also broken his silence after the win.
more: Burna Boy reportedly presented the Socrates Award to England's Bukayo Saka at the ceremony.
The win follows the earlier mix-up in which the winners were published online hours before the event.

stories.h: Court remands man accused of threatening to leak private images of Kano Governor Yusuf
stories.p: A Federal High Court in Abuja has reportedly ordered that Sanusi Dankaka be remanded over an alleged threat to leak private images of Governor Abba Yusuf. The case is said to be at an early stage.
more: The defendant has yet to be tried on the allegation.
The matter is expected to return to court at a later date.

stories.h: INEC publishes preliminary voters register online ahead of the 2027 election
stories.p: The Independent National Electoral Commission has put the preliminary voters register online, allowing Nigerians to check their details before the 2027 general election. The commission has said the national register is now above 103 million voters.
more: Voters can check that their names and polling units are correct.
Registration for new voters has run in several phases this year.

stories.h: Osimhen reportedly scores twice as Galatasaray win the Istanbul derby against Fenerbahce
stories.p: Victor Osimhen is reported to have scored two goals in Galatasaray's derby win over Fenerbahce, and the club's coach has since reacted to the result. Nigerian fans are celebrating the striker's performance online.
more: The match followed days of build-up around Osimhen's record against Fenerbahce.
Reactions from both sets of supporters are still coming in.
stories.alt: Victor Osimhen in a Lille kit
stories.credit: Photo: Liondartois / Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 4.0

stories.h: Gunmen reportedly abduct members of a security group linked to Sunday Igboho in Kwara
stories.p: Members of the Iru Ekun Security Group, which is associated with Yoruba nation agitator Sunday Igboho, were reportedly abducted by gunmen in Kwara State. Police have not yet said whether a rescue operation is under way.
more: The number of people taken has not been confirmed.
Kwara has seen several kidnapping incidents in recent months.
